sources.summary: Filippo Brunelleschi and the dome of Santa Maria del Fiore , completed in 1436 in the Italian city of Florence , represent an important chapter in the history of architecture, often associated with the growing distance between drawing and building. This separation, gradually consolidated over time, finds a decisive turning point in the Renaissance . Drawing becomes an instrument for anticipating and asserting authority over construction. The building site , once a space for invention and decision-making, came to be understood primarily as a place of execution.
